First, we find the values of $\theta $ for which the two curves intersect:

$$
\begin{aligned}2(1+\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ) & =1+\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  \\ 2+2\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  & =1+\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  & =-1\end{aligned}
$$

This gives us two solutions for $\theta \in [-\frac{\pi }{2},\frac{3\pi }{2}]:$

$$
\theta =-\frac{\pi }{2},\frac{3\pi }{2}
$$

To determine the inner function and the outer, let's draw an arrow from the origin that passes through the shaded region.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14248834/assets/d0ebb3b99f66e8c1af93f1a15ff4284f5fb9a83fb4d91bad1027e18c8b447939.png)

The arrow

- *enters* the region through the inner function $r=1+\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,$ and

- *leaves* through the outer function $r=2(1+\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ).$

To find the area, we use the formula

$$
A=\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{{\theta }_{1}}^{{\theta }_{2}}([\text{outer}]^{2}-[\text{inner}]^{2})\,\text{d}\theta ,
$$

where

$\,$ ${\theta }_{1}=-\frac{\pi }{2},\,$ and $\,{\theta }_{2}=\frac{3\pi }{2}.$

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{-\pi /2}^{3\pi /2}((2(1+\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ))^{2}-(1+\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta )^{2})\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =\frac{3}{2}{\int }_{-\pi /2}^{3\pi /2}(1+2\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta +{sin}^{2}⁡\theta )\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =\frac{3}{2}(\theta {|}_{-\pi /2}^{3\pi /2}-2\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta {|}_{-\pi /2}^{3\pi /2}+\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{-\pi /2}^{3\pi /2}(1-\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\theta ))\,\text{d}\theta ) \\  & =\frac{3}{2}((\frac{3\pi }{2}+\frac{\pi }{2})-2(0-0)+\frac{1}{2}\theta {|}_{-\pi /2}^{3\pi /2}-\frac{1}{4}\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\theta ){|}_{-\pi /2}^{3\pi /2}) \\  & =\frac{3}{2}(2\pi +\frac{1}{2}(\frac{3\pi }{2}+\frac{\pi }{2})-\frac{1}{4}(0-0)) \\  & =\frac{3}{2}(2\pi +\pi ) \\  & =\frac{9\pi }{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
